cases.threat: An attacker guesses credentials or distributes attempts across network sources.
cases.control: Argon2id verification, per-account lockout, and network-source throttling fail closed.
cases.recovery: A legitimate administrator waits for the bounded lockout or uses the separately controlled owner recovery path.
cases.testName: locks an account and throttles abusive network sources

cases.threat: A disabled or departed local user reuses an existing session while an attacker tries to remove the last owner.
cases.control: Account disablement revokes sessions and the final active owner cannot be disabled.
cases.recovery: An active owner restores an account deliberately; revoked sessions are never revived.
cases.testName: disables accounts, revokes sessions, and protects the final active owner

cases.threat: A browser creates a credential-bearing session over plaintext transport or a cross-origin request.
cases.control: Session creation requires HTTPS and exact same-origin validation.
cases.recovery: The request is rejected before a session exists and can be retried only through the trusted HTTPS origin.
cases.testName: requires HTTPS and same-origin before creating a browser session

cases.threat: A forged state-changing request or duplicated cookie attempts to confuse session selection.
cases.control: Host-only Secure cookies, unambiguous parsing, CSRF binding, expiry, and server-side revocation are mandatory.
cases.recovery: Invalid requests receive no mutation; sign-out or account disablement revokes the server-side session.
cases.testName: uses a host-only secure session cookie and rejects ambiguous duplicates

cases.threat: A registry, marketplace, or offline bundle substitutes a plugin signed by an untrusted or wrong publisher key.
cases.control: Canonical content and Ed25519 signatures are verified against active publisher-scoped trust before persistence.
cases.recovery: The candidate remains uninstalled; the administrator may import a newly signed immutable version after trust review.
cases.testName: verifies manifest and bundle Ed25519 signatures against publisher-scoped active trust

cases.threat: A plugin requests root, privileged mode, host namespaces, the Docker socket, or undeclared host mounts.
cases.control: The sandbox compiler denies and audits forbidden privileges before Node Agent staging.
cases.recovery: No container is started; only a new reviewed manifest with bounded permissions can be staged.
cases.testName: root, privileged, host namespace/network, Docker socket, and undeclared host mounts are denied and audited

cases.threat: Agent-generated code attempts a host escape through mounts, devices, namespaces, or runtime controls.
cases.control: Each user receives a non-root isolated sandbox without host mounts, Docker socket, direct devices, or GPU.
cases.recovery: The start is rejected before execution and the sandbox remains isolated for a corrected operation.
cases.testName: host escape controls and direct devices are denied before runtime start

cases.threat: A tool action is approved by the wrong actor, widened beyond its exact scope, or reused.
cases.control: Confirmation is authenticated, exact-scope, one-shot, expiring, audited, and never grants permanent approval.
cases.recovery: A denied or expired action requires a new scoped proposal and confirmation.
cases.testName: authenticated approval is exact-scope, one-shot, audited, and never grants always

cases.threat: A Bridge or OpenCode crash makes a side-effecting approval outcome uncertain and invites blind replay.
cases.control: Unknown outcomes are fenced as incomplete and automatic replay is forbidden.
cases.recovery: The user or administrator reconciles external state before issuing a new operation.
cases.testName: unknown approval outcome and crash require manual reconciliation without blind replay

cases.threat: Provider credentials or endpoints leak through administrator reads, metrics, or durable configuration.
cases.control: Credentials are stored only through protected ciphertext references and public projections are redacted.
cases.recovery: The credential can be rotated independently without exposing the prior secret or changing public routing identity.
cases.testName: administrator registration stores credentials only in protected ciphertext and returns redacted configuration

cases.threat: A failed external request is replayed after partial output and duplicates a visible result or side effect.
cases.control: The acceptance boundary and observed output fence blind failover and retry.
cases.recovery: The attempt remains incomplete until provider reconciliation establishes one authoritative result.
cases.testName: partial streamed output always blocks blind replay and requires provider reconciliation

cases.threat: A stolen object reference is used for another version, audience, operation, or after expiry.
cases.control: Signed references bind immutable version, audience, allowed operations, expiry, and live grant state.
cases.recovery: The reference is rejected; the authorized issuer must create a fresh narrowly scoped reference.
cases.testName: scoped references bind immutable version, audience, operations, expiry, and signature

cases.threat: A workload tries to read object bytes outside its user, operation, or current short-lived grant.
cases.control: Local workers receive only server-tracked operation-bound grants that can be revoked immediately.
cases.recovery: Revoking the grant blocks later reads; a new authorized request must obtain a new grant.
cases.testName: worker grants are short-lived, server-tracked, least-privilege, and immediately revocable

cases.threat: An upstream or cache supplies package bytes that do not match the approved digest.
cases.control: Artifacts are verified before caching and corrupted cache entries fail closed.
cases.recovery: The bad entry remains unavailable until trusted bytes matching immutable metadata are imported.
cases.testName: checksum mismatch and a corrupted cache fail closed

cases.threat: Removed offline media is silently treated as present, or a reattached disk inherits prior approval.
cases.control: Removal detaches the inventory immediately and attachment identity must be approved again.
cases.recovery: An administrator re-indexes and reapproves the current immutable media manifest.
cases.testName: disk removal immediately detaches approved inventory and reattachment requires reapproval

cases.threat: Another machine claims to be the appliance and submits misleading workload or health information.
cases.control: Only the installed local identity may report through the authenticated loopback service boundary.
cases.recovery: Reject the report without changing capacity or stopping any previously running local workload.
cases.testName: only the installed local identity can report appliance health

cases.threat: A browser forges internal identity headers or replays an earlier valid health report to change local availability.
cases.control: Internal identity is authenticated and bound to the exact request path, timestamp and single-use nonce.
cases.recovery: Reject forged and replayed requests without altering the appliance identity, capacity or guest state.
cases.testName: forged local gateway identity is rejected and valid reports cannot be replayed

cases.threat: A thief boots the appliance or moves its NVMe media and reaches protected services without an unlock factor.
cases.control: LOCKED deployment exposes only the minimal unlock surface and mounts no protected data service or volume.
cases.recovery: An authorized factor unlocks the data volume; no application service reads protected data beforehand.
cases.testName: LOCKED deployment exposes no protected data service or protected volume

cases.threat: A valid LUKS passphrase is retained in application state after Web unlock.
cases.control: The factor authenticates one bounded unlock and plaintext passphrase material is not retained.
cases.recovery: The passphrase can be rotated through the controlled key-slot lifecycle without persisting the old value.
cases.testName: correct LUKS passphrase factor authenticates one bounded unlock without retaining it

cases.threat: A lost USB factor cannot be revoked safely because recovery or the LUKS header operation fails.
cases.control: Offline recovery is separate and failed revocation restores an independently held header backup.
cases.recovery: The appliance remains in minimal recovery mode until the lost factor is revoked and a challenged replacement is enrolled.
cases.testName: lost USB revocation failure restores the independent header backup
